newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers' unions, employers to meet.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers' unions, employers to meet.

text.p: Unions and employers in the Italian engineering and metalworking industry will meet at 1100 GMT on Monday to see whether they can settle their protracted pay dispute, employers' group Federmeccanica said.

The group's director general, Michele Figurati, said the talks would take place at the Labour Ministry. "We will be sitting down to see if we can reach a deal," Figurati told reporters outside Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office.

Prodi met leaders of Italy's three main labour confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL and the employers' umbrella group Confindustria on Monday to try to give a final push to a settlement in the bitter dispute.
No talks have taken place between Federmeccanica and sectoral unions FIOM, FIM and UILM for several months.
The dispute, which has been accompanied by three one-day strikes since it began six months ago, affects 1.7 million workers in a sector that accounts for 40 percent of Italy's industrial output.
Any deal is likely to set the tone for other pay settlements and prove key to Italy's hopes of keeping a lid on inflation.
